s.description: Evaluate authentication and authorization patterns. Succinct, high-signal. Catches the things that get you breached.

scope.directories: auth/, middleware/, guards/, api/, routes/, lib/

spec_document.format:
## AuthN - Provider (Clerk, Auth0, Lucia, custom) - Token strategy (JWT, session, opaque) - Token storage (httpOnly cookie, memory -- NEVER localStorage) - Refresh strategy - MFA policy
## AuthZ - Model (RBAC, ABAC, ReBAC) - Permission matrix (role -> resource -> action) - Resource ownership rules - Elevation / sudo pattern - API-level enforcement point
## Session - Lifetime, rotation, revocation - Multi-device behavior - Concurrent session limits
## Secrets - Storage (env vars, Vault, CF secrets) - Rotation schedule - Never in code, never in logs

principles.principle: Every route is protected unless explicitly public. Allowlist, not blocklist.
Verify identity before checking permissions. Always.
Permission checks happen at route/middleware layer, not in business logic.
Every token, session, API key has minimum required scope.
Client is untrusted. Validate everything server-side. Client-side checks are UX, not security.

anti_patterns.violation: JWT/tokens stored in localStorage or sessionStorage (XSS = full account takeover)
No token expiry or infinite-lived tokens
Secrets in source code, .env committed, or logged
Password stored in plaintext or weak hash (MD5, SHA1 without salt)
Auth bypass: route accessible without authentication check
JWT signature not verified on every request
No CSRF protection on state-changing requests (if using cookies)
Token refresh without old token revocation (token accumulation)
User enumeration via login/signup error messages
No rate limiting on auth endpoints (brute force)
Session not invalidated on password change
No audit log for auth events
Missing Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite flags on auth cookies
IDOR: accessing resource by ID without ownership check (/api/users/123 returns any user)
Client-side only permission checks (no server enforcement)
Role check in business logic instead of middleware/guard
No resource-level authorization (role checked but not ownership)
Privilege escalation path: user can modify own role
Admin endpoints with no additional auth factor
Hardcoded role strings in permission checks
Inconsistent authz patterns across routes (some guarded, some not)
Permission denied returns different status than not-found (information leak)

criterion.name: Authentication Integrity
criterion.grade: Auth bypass exists; tokens in localStorage; secrets in code; plaintext passwords
Basic auth exists but gaps: missing expiry, no refresh rotation, user enumeration
Solid auth provider; tokens in httpOnly cookies; some gaps in refresh/revocation
Complete auth flow: secure storage, expiry, refresh rotation, CSRF, rate limiting
Hardened: MFA available, audit trail, session management, brute force protection, zero enumeration
Auth as zero-trust primitive; continuous verification; anomaly detection on auth patterns; passwordless primary; hardware key support

criterion.name: Authorization Model
criterion.grade: No authz; or client-side only; IDOR everywhere
Basic role checks but inline in business logic; no resource ownership
RBAC exists; middleware-based; but resource-level authz inconsistent
Clean RBAC + resource ownership; guards at route level; consistent
Policy engine (RBAC/ABAC); externalized rules; audit trail; zero authz in domain code
Relationship-based (ReBAC/Zanzibar); fine-grained; externalized; permission changes don't require deploys; authz is queryable and auditable in real-time

criterion.name: IDOR Prevention
criterion.grade: Resources fetched by ID with no ownership validation
Some ownership checks but not on all endpoints
Ownership checked on write paths; read paths exposed
All CRUD paths validate ownership or role; consistent pattern
Ownership enforced at repository/query layer; impossible to bypass at route level
Scoped queries: database queries inherently filtered by tenant/user; IDOR structurally impossible

criterion.name: Token Security
criterion.grade: localStorage; no expiry; no rotation; accumulation
HttpOnly cookies but long-lived; no refresh rotation
Short-lived access + refresh; rotation exists; some gaps
Proper token lifecycle: short access, rotating refresh, revocation on password change
Token binding; fingerprinting; concurrent session management; forced re-auth for sensitive ops
Cryptographic token binding to device; zero-extractable tokens; DPoP or equivalent

criterion.name: Secret Management
criterion.grade: Secrets in source code or committed .env files
Env vars but no rotation; some secrets logged accidentally
Proper env vars; rotation manual; log redaction exists
Secret manager (CF secrets, Vault); rotation policy; never in logs; never in error messages
Automated rotation; secret access audited; zero-trust secret delivery; test environments use separate secrets
Secrets are ephemeral; just-in-time delivery; automatic rotation; access anomaly detection

criterion.name: Defense in Depth
criterion.grade: Single layer of protection; one bypass = full access
Auth exists but no CSRF, no rate limiting, no input validation
Multiple layers but inconsistent (CSRF on some routes, not others)
Consistent: CSRF + rate limiting + input validation + CSP + CORS
All layers + security headers + request signing + anomaly detection
Security-in-depth as architecture: every layer independently secure; compromise of one layer doesn't cascade; penetration-tested regularly

example.description: The greatest hits of auth failures

standardization_check.step: Scan for routes without authentication middleware
Scan for DB queries by user-supplied ID without ownership filter
Scan for role/permission checks inside business logic (not guards)
Scan for secrets in source code (API keys, passwords, connection strings)
Verify CSRF protection on cookie-based auth
Verify rate limiting on auth endpoints
Verify token expiry and refresh rotation
